zeroModel.name: DeterministicAdmission
zeroModel.shape: CanonicalState + Candidate/Event + CurrentRule -> deterministic predicate/classification -> Admit/Reject/Result -> transition
sufficientWhen: relevant state/facts are already authoritative and directly available
classification predicate is closed enough for the case
no separately meaningful evidence dispute exists
no separately meaningful review/contestability relation is required

terms.workingTarget: an observer/system-relative acquisition or representation event
an observation, record, testimony, trace, artifact or derived representation admitted/relevant as support against a declared case question or claim under a procedure
a proposition/assertion whose status may be at issue or supplied as input
authoritative truth/state of the modeled underlying world at the queried scope when such truth is represented
a determination that some proposition is established/treated as the operative fact for the adjudicative case under current authority
text/code/form through which a norm/rule is represented
current authoritative rule/norm/standard/convention/evaluation basis admitted as governing or relevant to the case
overloaded family of semantic construal, norm construal, case characterization and relation-building; rejected as one atomic fixed stage
mapping a case/proposition/event/action/performance into one or more rule/evaluation-relevant categories or predicates
provenance-bearing basis by which evidence/norms/classifications/arguments support a determination; may be explicit, partial or opaque
case-level result whose status is binding/current within a declared Game/Practice scope because of admitted decision authority
transition/application that realizes a ruling through score/state/sanction/access/record/restart or other consequence
authorized process operating on a prior determination and possibly its evidence, interpretation, procedure, authority or scope
practice-recognized request/path invoking a review authority under specified standing/grounds/timing/procedure
derived property/topology of whether/how a current determination may be challenged, reviewed, modified or superseded under current practice
derived scoped/current property that no further admitted review/override path remains in the queried adjudicative horizon
derived history linking first-instance and later uphold/modify/reverse/supersede determinations with provenance/currentness
authoritative transition that supersedes/modifies a prior determination and prescribed current consequences/records as allowed by the practice

candidate Game-owned responsibility requiring enough separation among case question/target, admitted basis, current norm/evaluation basis, determination authority/result/provenance and review lineage to preserve player-relevant counterfactuals

Rationale is evidence by identity

Finality is correctness or truth

boundaryCases.case: deterministic digital action admission
boundaryCases.pressure: zero model succeeds; direct canonical state + closed predicate need not create explicit evidence/review machinery

boundaryCases.case: same WorldTruth, different/incomplete EvidenceBasis
boundaryCases.pressure: provisional/official case finding can vary while underlying represented truth stays fixed

boundaryCases.case: same observation, different case question
boundaryCases.pressure: what counts as relevant evidence depends on the declared claim/question/procedure

boundaryCases.case: same evidence + same rule text, different reasonable classification
boundaryCases.pressure: open-textured/standard-like predicate can leave interpretation/classification underdetermined by representation alone

boundaryCases.case: same classification, advisory analyst vs current referee/judge
boundaryCases.pressure: classification does not become binding without decision authority

boundaryCases.case: same authoritative ruling, different/failed enforcement
boundaryCases.pressure: ruling and effectuation remain separable

boundaryCases.case: IFAB final factual decision can still be mistaken
boundaryCases.pressure: finality/official case fact does not entail WorldTruth/correctness

boundaryCases.case: IFAB VAR review changes original decision
boundaryCases.pressure: review operates on prior determination; final decision lineage must preserve original and revised decision provenance

boundaryCases.case: IFAB post-incident sanction may persist after original decision changes
boundaryCases.pressure: reversal does not imply full rollback of all intervening consequences

boundaryCases.case: same decision, restart/review window differs
boundaryCases.pressure: contestability/finality varies with time/procedure while decision content stays fixed

boundaryCases.case: Magic floor-judge ruling appealed to Head Judge
boundaryCases.pressure: review/override can occur without treating appeal as a second independent first-instance case

boundaryCases.case: Magic Head Judge ruling has no further local appeal
boundaryCases.pressure: finality is review-topology-relative, not truth guarantee

boundaryCases.case: TTRPG open-intent outcome resolution
boundaryCases.pressure: player expression may require semantic construal + current rule/evaluation application before a GameAction/world consequence is admitted

boundaryCases.case: speedrun glitchless technique dispute
boundaryCases.pressure: category norm/predicate such as glitch can be practice-defined, contested and revised while executable mechanics stay fixed

boundaryCases.case: post-hoc speedrun record verification
boundaryCases.pressure: certification changes official practice record without rewriting historical run trajectory

boundaryCases.case: judged gymnastics with JSS support and Superior Jury review
boundaryCases.pressure: instrument/AI evidence support can improve classification while final adjudicative responsibility remains practice-assigned

boundaryCases.case: judged performance inquiry with unchanged performance
boundaryCases.pressure: score/difficulty recognition may change on review while physical performance history is unchanged

boundaryCases.case: natural-language companion command
boundaryCases.pressure: intent interpretation can be confidence/model-mediated and must not be equated with authoritative GameAction admission

boundaryCases.case: LLM game-rule understanding error
boundaryCases.pressure: fluent rule explanation/application can be semantically wrong; model output/confidence does not confer rule truth or authority

boundaryCases.case: generated rule proposal vs current authoritative norm
boundaryCases.pressure: generation/representation is candidate material until adopted by current rule authority

boundaryCases.case: new defeating evidence after an earlier justified determination
boundaryCases.pressure: adjudicative reasoning can be defeasible/non-monotonic; more evidence can rationally reverse a prior conclusion

boundaryCases.case: same Agent proposes action, interprets intent and adjudicates legality
boundaryCases.pressure: single model identity does not collapse proposal/evidence/reasoning/decision provenance; practice may impose separation constraints

boundaryCases.case: moderation case with policy ambiguity
boundaryCases.pressure: content observation + policy text may require case classification and authority; enforcement can be delayed or independently reviewed

boundaryCases.case: review without new evidence but changed norm interpretation
boundaryCases.pressure: review is not reducible to evidence replay; decision can change because applicable interpretation/classification changes

externalAnchors.claim: referee decisions can be final within match authority while referees can make mistakes; VAR review is scoped; final decision belongs to referee; reversal need not cancel all post-incident discipline
first-instance judge rulings, Head Judge appeal/finality and official tournament procedure separate review from first-instance adjudication
running-game guidance explicitly includes resolving outcomes, consequences and improvising answers, providing an open/facilitated resolution regime
glitchless speedrun rules expose contested category predicates and community/practice adjudication beyond executable mechanics
technology/AI outputs support inquiry/blocked-score review while Superior Jury retains practice-level decision role
LLMs can make errors in applying/interacting with/evaluating game rules; rule fluency is not semantic correctness
language game companions use confidence-based interpretation of complex player commands, demonstrating intent interpretation as a distinct layer
defeasible/non-monotonic reasoning provides a cross-disciplinary falsifier for monotonic evidence-to-decision assumptions
